reasoning_traces.think:
The Champion/Challenger framework implements a rigorous statistical hypothesis test to prevent overfitting. It requires the challenger model to demonstrate a minimum Brier score reduction (e.g., 1.5%) while maintaining out-of-sample performance within a tolerance band (e.g., 3% worse than in-sample). This dual-threshold rule ensures that promotions occur only when the new model provides genuine predictive improvements rather than spurious correlations. The closed-line value (CLV) serves as the primary economic objective, directly linking model selection to betting profits. By enforcing a frozen champion policy, the system avoids frequent switching that could destabilize trading strategies due to parameter estimation error. The promotion decision acts as a veto gate, rejecting challengers whose out-of-sample performance fails to meet the required significance level.
